summary: A Great Bay Spa & Sauna blog post (April 27, 2023) explaining why hot tub water needs continuous circulation via a circulation pump attached to the filter. It covers the benefits of circulation for water quality, sanitation and energy use, lists signs of poor circulation with troubleshooting steps (hard water, dirty filter, air in the line, pump malfunction), and notes the annual replacement need for the ClearRay UV-C bulb. It closes by encouraging readers to add a circulation pump or contact the company for maintenance.
one_line: A hot tub blog post explaining why water circulation pumps should run constantly and how to troubleshoot poor circulation.
key_facts: The blog post 'Understanding the Importance of Water Circulation' by Great Bay Spa & Sauna is dated April 27, 2023 and has an estimated reading time of 4 minutes.
A circulation pump attaches to the hot tub filter and keeps hot tub water moving between uses and between water replacements.
Hot tubs use two types of water circulation: jet pumps, which circulate water faster while bathing, and circulation pumps, which run at low speed between uses.
Stagnant water is more prone to bacteria growth and buildup, which can lead to more cleaning and maintenance work.

The article recommends running the circulation pump constantly, because doing so avoids surface bacteria growth, removes harmful particles, and keeps water warmer so it takes less time and energy to heat up.

Signs of poor water circulation include algae or dirt on top of the water, cloudier than usual water, little or no water movement through the filter, too much noise, and an error code or light on the circulation pump.
Hard water can cause calcium or lime deposits on the pump, which can make loud noises or stop it from working; cloudy water can be a sign of hard water.
If the filter looks damaged or clogged, it should be cleaned or replaced depending on its condition.
Air caught in the pump lines can cause louder than normal sounds; pumps with an air bleeder knob can release air by loosening the knob.
A well-maintained pump should last five to ten years, if not longer.
The article advises unplugging the pump before diagnosing it to prevent further damage and avoid injury.
ClearRay Active Oxygen Technology is a water disinfectant system used in Sundance Spas hot tubs that uses UV-C light to destroy contaminants and waterborne pathogens.
According to the article, 99.9% of water-borne bacterial and viral DNA is destroyed once water enters the ClearRay System.
The ClearRay bulb should be replaced annually to maintain its effectiveness.
Great Bay Spa & Sauna has a showroom at 1850 Woodbury Ave, Portsmouth, NH 03801 and describes itself as the hot tub, swim spa, and sauna experts in Portsmouth and all of New England.
